title: SAML 2.0 guided federation onboarding with tolerant metadata ingestion and admin dry-run
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a resilient SAML 2.0 federation onboarding flow that focuses on tolerant metadata ingestion, an admin dry-run approval surface, and end-to-end auditability. Many customers fail to onboard because IdP metadata contains nonstandard attributes, unexpected XML namespaces, or missing optional elements. This ticket proposes: (1) a tolerant ingestion pipeline that normalizes and canonicalizes incoming metadata while preserving the original artifact for audit; (2) a dry-run mode that validates and surfaces issues with suggested fixes without committing changes; (3) an admin approval step gated by RBAC v2 roles; and (4) comprehensive audit logging of raw metadata, normalization diffs, validation verdicts, and the admin decision. The implementation must be backward compatible with existing connector APIs and provide toggles for strict vs tolerant modes for enterprise customers with stricter compliance needs.
acceptance_criteria: Inbound SAML metadata can be uploaded via console, API, or remote MDQ URL and enters a dry-run validation pipeline without altering live connector config.
Dry-run returns a structured report: errors, warnings, suggested fixes, and normalized preview. Report stored in audit logs alongside original payload.
Only users with the RBAC v2 role 'security-admin' or higher can confirm and commit metadata changes; others can request approval.
All ingestion steps emit audit events with immutable IDs, timestamps, and KMS-signed digests for tamper evidence.
Fuzz-test corpus of 1k real-world IdP metadata files runs with <1% unhandled parser crashes and a measurable drop in false-negative validation rejections vs current parser baseline.
Feature behind feature-flag 'saml_tolerant_ingest' with canary rollout plan; metrics and SLOs defined before global enablement.
tasks: Build tolerant XML ingestion layer (canonicalize, whitelist namespaces, preserve unknown attrs)
Add dry-run API that returns structured validation reports and normalized preview
Wire dry-run -> admin approval flow with RBAC v2 gating and optional approval requests
Emit audit events at each pipeline stage and store original payload in immutable audit store
Create fuzz-test harness and run against historical metadata corpus; iterate parser heuristics
Add feature-flag and rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%) with metrics dashboard
comments: 2025-02-16 Maya Patel: Initial proposal posted. Called out common failure modes (nonstandard EntityDescriptor, duplicate entityID, unexpected X509 encodings). Recommended keeping original raw metadata in audit store for forensics.

2025-02-18 Ethan Zhao: Architecture review notes — prefer existing canonicalization lib used by saml-parser repo to reduce dependency surface. Concern about performance impact; propose streaming validation to keep memory bounded.

2025-02-24 Security Review (Anjali Rao): Approved conceptually. Requirement: store signer info and KMS digest; enable strict mode for customers with compliance requirements. Also suggested retention policy for raw payloads (90 days by default).
2025-02-28 Design feedback (Luca Marino): UI should emphasize 'Dry-run' clearly and show diffs inline; include 'Accept suggested fixes' quick action to reduce admin friction.

2025-03-03 QA (Priya Nair): Fuzz harness ran 1k corpus; parser crashed 7 times on malformed namespaces — added defensive checks and re-ran; crashes resolved. Current validation_fail_rate metric baseline set to 0.8%.

2025-03-05 Ethan Zhao: Implemented dry-run API endpoint and audit event schema. Pushed initial PRs for parser changes and audit-store. Manual QA with a partner customer successful. Next: RBAC gating integration and canary rollout config.
audit_plan: Store original metadata blob in immutable audit store (WORM style) with KMS-signed sha256 digest. Log events: ingestion_received, normalized_preview_generated, validation_report_emitted, approval_requested, approval_granted, commit_applied. Retention default 90 days, configurable per org. Audit exports to SIEM (splunk/seq) supported.
qa_plan: Create corpus from historical customer metadata (anonymized), including common vendor IdPs. Run fuzz harness with incremental parser heuristics. Verify: dry-run reports map 95% of warnings to suggested fixes; admin commit flow preserves previous connector config as rollback snapshot.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged. Canary to 5% of orgs for 72 hours. Monitor parser crash rate and validation_fail_rate. If stable, expand to 25% for one week, then 100%. Provide 'strict mode' toggle per org for compliance customers.
release_notes: Adds a tolerant SAML metadata dry-run onboarding flow that surfaces validation issues, suggests fixes, and requires RBAC v2 approval to commit. Audit logs now include raw metadata and normalization diffs. Feature is behind a feature flag and will be rolled out gradually.
implementation_constraints: Must reuse saml-parser library v2.1 for canonicalization to reduce maintenance. Avoid storing unencrypted PII in audit store; redact NameID/text fields per data retention policy. Keep memory usage bounded by streaming parsing.
security_considerations: Validate XML external entity (XXE) protection enabled. Reject metadata with embedded remote references unless explicitly allowed via MDQ with TLS. KMS-backed digests for tamper detection. Approval action must be auditable and require RBAC v2 permission.
